title: Asynchronous Telemetry Gating and Traffic-Shed Strategy for Platform Observability
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This document defines Redwood’s standard for adaptive telemetry gating and traffic-shed behavior for the platform control plane and inference runtime. The goal is to preserve actionable observability while bounding ingest cost and avoiding monitoring-induced cascades during high-load or failure modes. It applies to all platform telemetry producers: runtime agents, API gateways, dedicated pool controllers, and customer-facing routers.

Why this matters:
- Telemetry itself can become a source of load (high-cardinality traces, heavy span emission, verbose debug logs).
- During incidents, uncontrolled telemetry growth increases downstream latency, bloats storage, and can worsen customer-facing SLOs.
- We need a deterministic, reversible way to reduce telemetry volume while retaining critical signals for remediation and postmortem.

Scope and definitions:
- Gate: a configurable, runtime-enabled rule that reduces or transforms telemetry emitted by a service (example: drop non-error traces, reduce sampling rate, redact high-cardinality fields).
- Shed: temporary, automatic reduction of inbound request traffic to downstream consumers (eg. metrics pipeline, trace collector) under overload conditions.
- Tiered signal categories:
  - Critical signals: errors with customer impact, core SLO breaches, control-plane state changes (must be preserved).
  - Operational signals: high-resolution latency histograms, traces used for triage (preferred to preserve but can be throttled).
  - Diagnostic signals: debug logs, verbose span details, high-cardinality fields (can be gated aggressively).

Ownership and teams:
- Owner: eng-platform (primary), eng-sre (secondary) — responsible for global gating policies and tooling.
- Service owners: each service must implement the standard client libraries and honor gating decisions (see rollout checklist).
- Observability infra: observability team operates the ingest-side policies (collector, samplers, retention) and provides dashboards to track gating impact.

SLOs and thresholds we protect:
- Control-plane API p95 latency: target <= 120ms, SLO 99.5%/30d
- Inference routing 99th percentile token latency: target <= 400ms, SLO 99%/30d (customer-facing)
- Telemetry pipeline ingestion lag: target <= 30s, alert if > 60s for 5m
The gating system must reduce telemetry ingest to keep pipeline ingestion lag under alert threshold.

High-level architecture (text diagram):
- Instrumented service -> local SDK (adaptive sampler + gate client) -> agent/collector -> central router -> storage/analysis systems
- Central control plane exposes runtime gate decisions via: 1) feature flag push (repos: ff-proxy), 2) pub/sub control topic (kafka/arn), 3) HTTP pull endpoint for low-latency overrides.

Runtime behaviors and priorities (ordered):
1. Circuit-grade safety: if the collector reports ingestion-backpressure or high-lag, central controller triggers a conservative shed across all agents (global "emergency-shed" policy).
2. Priority preserving: always preserve Critical signals even during emergency-shed.
3. Graceful degradation: drop Diagnostic signals first, then progressively reduce Operational signals (e.g., reduce trace sampling from 10%->1%->0.1%).
4. Scoped application: policies can be applied by namespace, service, environment (prod/stage), or by tenant (priority tenant slicing).

Policy examples (JSON examples shown as pseudo-config in docs):
- Global emergency-shed policy (applied when pipeline_lag > 60s for 2m):
  - preserve: ["error_events", "control_plane_state_change"]
  - traces_sample_rate: 0.001
  - log_level_min: "WARN"
  - redact_fields: ["user_input.text", "request.headers.x-session-id"]

- Cost-conservative day policy (non-incident):
  - preserve: ["error_events"]
  - traces_sample_rate: 0.02
  - log_level_min: "INFO"

Collector-side thresholds (PromQL examples):
- Ingestion lag alert:
  - promql: |
     max_over_time(collector_ingestion_lag_seconds[5m]) > 60
  - alert: CollectorIngestLagHigh (SEV-3)

- High-cardinality trace volume (example query):
  - promql: |
     sum(rate(trace_spans_emitted_total[1m])) by (service) > 1000
  - action: consider reducing per-service sample rate

Local SDK behavior (must be implemented by service owners):
- SDK reads latest gate config from local cache; fallback to last-known-good config if controller is unreachable.
- When gate indicates reduced sampling, SDK must apply deterministic sampling (hash-based) for traces and metrics to preserve reproducibility in rollouts and debugging.
- SDK provides a local override API for operator e2e tests (disabled by default in prod).

Operational runbook: when alerts indicate telemetry/backpressure issues:
1. Pager: CollectorIngestLagHigh -> notify oncall observability and eng-platform on same page.
2. Triage: observe pipeline lag, check broker (kafka) lag, and verify collector CPU/IO.
3. If lag persists > 5m, engage global emergency-shed:
   a. Open Gate Console (internal: /gate-console) and enable emergency-shed (automated button).
   b. Confirm preserve list contains "error_events" and "control_plane_state_change".
   c. Apply redaction rules for any PII fields discovered in active logs.
4. Route: notify service owners of each top contributor (via top_n by emitted_spans metric).
5. After stabilization (lag < 30s for 10m), progressively relax gates in reverse order and monitor for recurrence.

Dashboard panels and queries to include (minimum):
- Collector ingestion lag (time series, 1h/6h/24h) with alert band overlay.
- Emitted spans by service (top 20) with per-service sample rate.
- Storage ingress bytes per hour and projected 30d burn-rate estimate.
- Emergency-shed state timeline (annotation stream).
- Critical-signal delivery rate (sanity check that critical signals are still flowing).

Alert routing and escalation:
- SEV-1 (system-wide pipeline outage): page oncall (paging window per incident policy), eng-platform lead, SRE director.
- SEV-2 (sustained ingestion lag > 60s): page observability oncall + service owners for top contributors.
- SEV-3 (spike in trace emission from a single tenant): notify affected service owner and customer success if customer impact suspected.

Rollout checklist for services (must be completed before a service goes to prod):
1. Integrate Redwood telemetry SDK and feature-flag client (library: telemetry-client v2.4+).
2. Add unit tests for deterministic sampling behavior.
3. Add config UI hints in service manifest (annotations: telemetry.policy).
4. Run staged canary for 72 hours in staging env with sample_rate=0.02 and verify dataset quality.
5. Sign-off from eng-sre and observability.

Testing and verification exercises (gamedays):
- Scenario A: burst of 10x trace volume from a non-critical background job. Verify emergency-shed triggers and critical signals persist.
- Scenario B: persistent moderate increase in cardinality. Measure cost delta and tune day-policy sampling.

Post-incident analysis and metrics to capture in retrospectives:
- Time to detect: time from first lag metric > 60s to emergency-shed activation.
- Time to stabilize: time from shed activation to ingestion lag < 30s.
- Lost signal analysis: number of traces/logs dropped per category; note any missing critical signals and root cause.

Implementation notes and constraints:
- Deterministic hashing for sampling must use stable seed per deploy to avoid churn across restarts.
- Redaction must be applied before any externally-shared telemetry to guard PII.
- Producers must not embed unbounded high-cardinality fields in span attributes; these should be mapped to tags with cardinality guards.

Appendix: quick CLI and API examples
- Check current global gate state (curl):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $GATE_TOKEN" https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/gates/global/state

- Force enable emergency-shed (for runbook use only):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $GATE_TOKEN" -d '{"policy":"emergency-shed","actor":"oncall","reason":"CollectorIngestLagHigh"}' https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/gates/override

- Example deterministic sampler pseudo-code (python):
  def should_sample(trace_id, sample_rate):
      h = int(hashlib.sha256(trace_id.encode()).hexdigest(), 16) % 1000000
      return (h / 1000000.0) < sample_rate
